constitution.principle: Time alone never changes a KORAL.
Data arrival alone never changes a KORAL.
Evidence-confidence change is not organizational change.
A Material Change requires a canonical organizational-state transition.
Reversal creates history; it does not erase it.
Advisor interprets/confirms only where allowed; never draws KORAL.
Company preserves/uses states; never manipulates morphology.
Worker-level/private data never enters outward morphology.
Under-recognition is safer than false visual change.
Decision Pack alone can never create RECOGNIZED Material Change.
Expression Mode is mandatory before outward/Worker-facing distribution.
Persistent/public/physical artifacts derive from an authorized Edition state unless a future explicit exception is justified.

materialChangeTaxonomy.organizationalPhenomenon: A new organizational element appears (a new initiative area, a new Need recognized)
materialChangeTaxonomy.justifyingEvidence: Initiative created + published; Need Hypothesis created
materialChangeTaxonomy.insufficientEvidence: A single mention in Advisor free text alone

materialChangeTaxonomy.organizationalPhenomenon: An organizational element ends (initiative closes, Assignment ends, a Need is no longer pursued)
materialChangeTaxonomy.insufficientEvidence: A gap in activity with no closing event

materialChangeTaxonomy.organizationalPhenomenon: An area gains more organizational weight (Need moves Hypothesis→Emerging→Supported)
materialChangeTaxonomy.justifyingEvidence: Classification transition with new supporting evidence
materialChangeTaxonomy.insufficientEvidence: Increased volume of the same evidence (see organizationChangedVsKoraLearned type B, Evidence update)
materialChangeTaxonomy.notes: Morphology ONLY if classification actually transitions — never on repeated confirmation of an already-reached classification.

materialChangeTaxonomy.organizationalPhenomenon: An area loses organizational weight without fully disappearing (activity continues but a Need reclassifies toward Insufficient-Evidence-Unknown)
materialChangeTaxonomy.insufficientEvidence: Silence (absence of new evidence is not evidence of weakening)

materialChangeTaxonomy.organizationalPhenomenon: Multiple smaller elements resolve into fewer, clearer ones (several related initiatives close in favor of one broader one; several ambiguous Needs resolve into one Supported Need)
materialChangeTaxonomy.insufficientEvidence: An unrelated cluster of closures with no coordinating evidence
materialChangeTaxonomy.notes: Explicitly non-negative — consolidation is a neutral, valid transformation (constitution principle 7), never treated as decline.

materialChangeTaxonomy.organizationalPhenomenon: Direction changes without simple growth/shrinkage (a Need's statement/domain shifts, an initiative's scope changes)
materialChangeTaxonomy.justifyingEvidence: Initiative scope change (if tracked); new Decision Pack superseding a prior one's direction

materialChangeTaxonomy.organizationalPhenomenon: An area that was uncertain settles into a confirmed, unchanging state
materialChangeTaxonomy.justifyingEvidence: Sustained Supported classification across multiple periods, no new contradicting evidence
materialChangeTaxonomy.notes: Reversibility is not applicable — stabilization IS the stable state itself. Represented as a 'settled' region marker plus a confidence dimension.

materialChangeTaxonomyNote: Retained set for Change Protocol v1: exactly these seven categories, all directly attestable by real KORA objects today or in the near-term roadmap. Fragmentation, Differentiation, Convergence, Structural discontinuity, and Uncertainty revision were considered and explicitly excluded from this taxonomy (doc 129 Part 2) — not because they are meaningless, but because no supporting canonical KORA object currently expresses them (Fragmentation/Differentiation/Convergence), or because they belong to a different, later mechanism (Structural discontinuity → Continuity Contract, KORA-WP-113; Uncertainty revision → confidence-only, never morphology, never a Material Change Event on its own).

organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.name: Real organizational transformation
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.koraExample: An initiative is formally closed; an Advisor Assignment ends; a Decision Pack is published enacting a new direction

organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.name: Evidence update
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.definition: New evidence arrives about something already believed
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.koraExample: A second, independent Advisor observation supports an already-Supported Need — same conclusion, more proof

organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.name: Interpretation update
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.definition: The same evidence is read differently (by KORA logic or Advisor) without new facts
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.koraExample: An Advisor revises their read of an existing Case's significance

organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.name: Data correction
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.definition: A prior record was simply wrong and is fixed
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.koraExample: A tenant_code typo corrected; a misattributed initiative pillar fixed

organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.name: Confidence update
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.definition: The Confidence Score / calibration shifts due to broader data completeness, unrelated to any one fact
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.koraExample: Overall tenant confidence_score rises because more UEF records were approved this period

organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.name: No material change
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.definition: Nothing meets any of the above at a level worth recording
organizationChangedVsKoraLearned.koraExample: Routine appointment scheduling; a Case opened and resolved with no new organizational fact

organizationChangedVsKoraLearnedNote: Only type A ever justifies a Material Change Event (doc 129 Part 3, verbatim: 'Only A ever justifies a Material Change Event. B, D, and E must never touch morphology — they are Evidence/Trust Layer concerns exclusively.'). Type C is explicitly named as the most dangerous category — it can feel like organizational change without any underlying fact changing; the Change Protocol must require a canonical object transition, never merely a changed interpretation, before recognizing anything from category C.
